audit.whatIsWrong: The lane-difficulty framing is internally inconsistent: breakdown.difficulty says 7.5/10 and breakdown.carry says 7.5/10 while diffRating says 5.5/10 and carryRating 6/10, and the level chart marks Levels 4-5 as 'Skill' even though its own why says Darius grinds him down every walk-up.
audit.why: Darius holds a 55.18% win rate over 4393 Emerald+ games and the packet levelChart is Darius/Darius/Darius/Darius/Darius/Skill/Yone. Levels 4-5 is a Darius stage, not a coin flip; the coin flip is the first-item stage.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 flipped to Darius (7/10). Difficulty and carry prose left alone this pass because the numeric mismatch spans a champion-level field pair — flagged in questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ item stage is marked Darius (8/10) in both layers while whys[6] says Yone's crit spike flips the matchup — the chart and its own explanation say opposite things. Spike text also credits Yone with a 'double-dash R'.
audit.why: Fate Sealed is a single blink behind the last champion in a line; there is no second dash. Yone's real late spike is crit items plus Spirit Cleave, whose cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed (14s base), and Soul Unbound falling to 10s at rank 5.
audit.corrected: 2+ items flipped to Yone (4/10); phases[6].why, whys[6], late, spikes[3].text and wants.foe[2] rewritten around the crit spike, the attack-speed-scaled Spirit Cleave shield and the 10s Soul Unbound.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fate Sealed is described three separate times as a disengage/kiting/dodge tool ('gap-closing dash-through that can dodge your ult', 'let him disengage or reset', 'double-dash R lets him kite your slows'). It is the opposite.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Yone blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him.' It closes distance and drags you with him — into Apprehend's 535 range and Noxian Guillotine's 460 range. Yone's actual escape is Soul Unbound, which forces his spirit back to his body when it ends, so the body marks his landing spot.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[1], spikes[2], spikes[3], late, whys[6], report[5] and tldr around: Fate Sealed pulls you toward him rather than away; Soul Unbound (22s rank 1 to 10s rank 5) is the cooldown that decides commits; Mortal Steel only dashes and knocks up on the third cast (4s cooldown, 450 range vs Apprehend's 535).
sources: enemyKit Q/E/R Riot text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1], dontsFull[1] and dontsFull[2] have titles that do not match their bodies — 'Dodge his Q3' is paired with generic trade advice, 'Fight during his E burst' with Apprehend advice, 'Extend into his R' with Apprehend advice again.
audit.why: Each body was copy-pasted from tradeGood/tradeBad, so three of the six trigger cards teach nothing about the trigger they name.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to match their headings: Mortal Steel's third-cast rule, Soul Unbound repeating spirit-form damage on the snap-back, and Fate Sealed's 1000 range dragging you under tower.

audit.why: Soul Unbound is correctly named as the matchup-defining cooldown; the audit only added the real numbers (22/19/16/13/10) so the advice is countable rather than vague.

edits.before: Sidestep his third linear Q wind dash, camp his physical anchor return portal on the ground to secure a free combo, and chase with Ghost.
edits.after: Sidestep the third Mortal Steel — that one dashes and knocks up. Soul Unbound snaps him back to his body, so stand on the body and combo him there.

edits.before: Sidestep his third linear Q wind dash, camp his physical anchor return portal on the ground to secure a free combo, and chase with Ghost.
edits.after: Sidestep the third Mortal Steel — that one dashes and knocks up. Soul Unbound snaps him back to his body, so stand on the body and combo him there.

edits.before: You stay a side-lane terror but fall off vs grouped teams. Look for flank pulls in fights; one reset chain can win the game.
edits.after: Yone's crit items and attack-speed-scaled Spirit Cleave shield out-scale you; he kites in the open. Fight only in the side lane.

edits.before: Level 3 E Apprehend cancels his Q-dashes and there's no Windwall to save him.
edits.after: Level 3 Apprehend reaches 535 — further than his 450-range Mortal Steel.

edits.before: Late, Yone's crit spike, Q3 interrupt and double-dash dive kiting flip the matchup.
edits.after: Late, Yone's crit spike, Q3 knockup and a faster Spirit Cleave shield flip the matchup.

edits.before: At 5 stacks R Noxian Guillotine resets and executes him — but Yone's R Fate Sealed is a gap-closing dash-through that can dodge your ult or set up his own all-in, so time your Guillotine on his cooldown, not into his.
edits.after: At 5 stacks Noxian Guillotine executes him and resets on the kill — his answer is Soul Unbound, not Fate Sealed, since Fate Sealed blinks him behind you and drags you along. Ult when his E is spent, not before.

edits.before: This is the coin-flip: your E-pull answers his E Soul Unbound recall window (bait him to spend E, then all-in the ghost's return spot), while his Q3 knockup plus R let him disengage or reset — outcome hinges on who lands their key cast first.
edits.after: The coin-flip window: bait Soul Unbound (22s at rank 1, 10s at rank 5), then all-in where his body sits, because that is where he lands. Fate Sealed is not an escape — it drags you toward him, straight into Apprehend and R range.

edits.before: With bruiser-crit items (Guinsoo/IE) Yone's Q3 knockup, E-return burst and double-dash R let him kite your slows and dive over you; his airborne on Q3 interrupts your R animation, tilting extended fights his way.
edits.after: With crit items Yone's Q3 knockup and Soul Unbound carry him: attack speed cuts Spirit Cleave's 14s shield cooldown, so he can absorb your burst twice in one fight. Kill him before the second shield lands.

edits.before: After his first crit item the lane balances then tips: his Q3 knockup interrupts your ult, E Soul Unbound gives a free burst window, and double-dash R lets him kite your slows and dive immobile Darius.
edits.after: After his first crit item the lane tips: Soul Unbound drops to 13-10s so his escape is almost always up, and Spirit Cleave's shield refreshes faster with attack speed. Force fights in the side lane, not the open map.

edits.before: Reach crit spike to kite slows and dive with double-dash R
edits.after: Reach the crit spike and reset fights with Soul Unbound

edits.before: Pull Yone as he steps to last-hit, W slow, land the Q outer ring, weave two autos, and walk away at 3-4 stacks with the heal banked.
edits.after: Mortal Steel is a 4s cooldown, and only the third cast dashes and knocks up. Sidestep that one and his knockup is gone for two more Q casts.

edits.before: Your committal tool is the lane — burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Soul Unbound repeats a share of his spirit-form damage when it ends. Trade after that snap, not into it.

edits.before: Whiffing Apprehend and then fighting anyway — without the pull you have no engage, and chasing through a wave bleeds you dry.
edits.after: Fate Sealed reaches 1000 units and drags you to him — past the wave he yanks you under tower or into a waiting jungler.

edits.before: Track Yone's Soul Unbound: He snaps back when it ends. Pull him there. Engage only while it is down.
edits.after: Soul Unbound: 22s early, 10s maxed. He returns to his body — stand on it. Fate Sealed pulls you in, not away.

notes: Level chart flipped as one group across both layers: Levels 4-5 Skill->Darius (5/10->7/10) and 2+ items Darius->Yone (8/10->4/10), matching the packet levelChart and the existing whys[3]/whys[6] text, which already described those stages the way the packet does. The recurring 'double-dash R' / 'R dodges your ult' claim about Fate Sealed is false in three places and is corrected — Riot's text has it blink behind the last champion in a line and pull enemies toward him. Claims I did NOT touch because the kits cannot settle them: whether Apprehend's pull interrupts a Mortal Steel dash mid-flight, and whether Yone's Q3 airborne interrupts Noxian Guillotine's leap. Both are left as-is on the page and listed in unverified.
